3.  25-55719  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Housing, Assistance and
  Prevention (HHAP) Round 6 presentation from the Health Department.

  • Homeless Services Administrative Officer Jeffrey Proctor presented an
  overview on Housing, Assistance and Prevention (HHAP) Program- Round,
  the presentation included the current status of homeless service systems
  and system needs. Staff would like to receive feedback on the value of CoC
  programs and services.
  • HHAP funding represents approximately 10% of the annual budget for the
  Long Beach CoC and Homeless Services. To help maintain the expanded
  services currently in place, continued funding is essential—State HHAP
  Round 6 will play a critical role in sustaining these efforts.
  • The $1 billion block grant program, authorized under Section 13 of AB 166
  and signed into law by Governor Newsom on July 2, 2024, will provide
  significant funding across the state. The City of Long Beach is expected to
  receive $8,227,243, with $4,114,344 allocated specifically to the Long Beach
  Continuum of Care (CoC).
  • The application process will be completed as a region, all continuum's of
  care within the County of Los Angeles shall be considered part of a single
  region.
  • The Long Beach CoC proposed fund priorities for HHAP 6 include Rapid
  Rehousing and Shallow Subsidy, Interim Housing Operating funds and
  Transition Age Youth Services.
  • City staff and board members engaged in a discussion following the
  presentation. Board members expressed concerns about potential medical
  budget cuts and the long-term sustainability of funding.
  • A member of the public shared concerns about youth exiting the foster care
  system and expressed interest in connecting with board members who have
  more information or expertise on the topic.

4.  25-55725  Recommendation to receive and file the HUD CoC Waiver Guidance presentation
  from the Health Department.

  • Health department staff member Cassandra Bonney provided an overview of
  ESG, ESG-RUSH, and CoC Federal Waivers. HUD released a Memorandum
  of Understanding (MOU) for these waivers on January 8, 2025. The city
  applied for these waivers to offer additional support to individuals and
  families affected by disasters or emergencies.
  • The HUD waivers provide greater flexibility, reduce barriers, and expedite
  housing placements, while supporting system-wide adaptation. These
  waivers will enable the Long Beach CoC to maintain housing stability, ease
  access to federally restricted funds, and respond more effectively to
  emergencies.
  • The Homeless Services Bureau applied for 10 federal waivers, waivers are
  temporary and will expire February 4, 2027.
  • Subrecipients are not required to request approval or notify HSB when
  implementing applicable waivers in their programs. While these waivers
  remain in effect, they take precedence over the Long Beach CoC Written
  Standards and the CoC’s Policies and Procedures.
  • During the meeting, Member Aiko asked staff whether the city has seen a
  significant number of individuals affected by the recent fires.

  A motion was made by Member Scott, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Lock, Lowery-Luyties, Tan,
  Topolewski, Scott, Shuford

5.  25-55720  Recommendation to receive and file a discussion on the Continuum of Care Builds
  (CoC Builds) Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) updates by HUD.

  • Homeless Services Administrative Officer Jeffrey Proctor provided a verbal
  update regarding the upcoming fall presentation for the CoC Builds NOFO.
  Century was previously selected as the applicant through the original RFP
  process. However, in April, the City received notice from HUD indicating that
  the RFP would be withdrawn and re-released at a later date.
  • The city has resubmitted an application for the RFP, similar to the original
  one previously submitted. There have been some updates to the NOFO
  regarding equity changes. HUD is now prioritizing awards for Continuums of
  Care (CoC) serving populations under 2 million people. We will provide
  further updates as more information becomes available.

  A motion was made by Member Lock, seconded by Member Boyce, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  10 Amick, Boyce, Brown-Shock, Diles III, Lock, Lowery-Luyties, Tan,
  Topolewski, Scott, Shuford
  No:  0 None

6.  25-55721  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff and
  Operations Update presentation from the Health Department.

  • Homeless Services Administrative Officer Jeffrey Proctor provided the staff
  operations updates, including the encampment resolution round 2, non-
  congregate shelter closed out on May 30. On May 29 the US Department of
  Labor reported it would be ceasing the Job Corp centers across the
  Country.
  • Prop 1 Behavorial Health Capitol Improvement Project awards were
  announced on May 12, no projects in Long Beach were awarded.
  • The city hosted its first Housing and Homelessness Opportunities,
  Mobilization and Engagement Community Roadshow events June 12.
  • The CoC has received notice that Harbor Interfaith will serve as the new
  screening point of contact for families moving forward. Additionally, HSB will
  be releasing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for organizations interested in
  providing non-congregate shelter services under ERF 3. The non-congregate
  shelter is expected to serve approximately 60 individuals.
